title: Attention kernel eviction emulator and startup fallback procedure
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: We observed increased decode tail-latency and sporadic OOMs for a subset of long-context workloads after rolling FlashAttention v3 kernels behind the kernel-selector. This ticket builds an "eviction emulator" test harness that can reproduce GPU workspace eviction and warmup timing at small scale, so we can reason about prefill->decode handoff and define a robust startup fallback procedure.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro harness reproduces observed tail-latency spike locally and in CI with <5% variance across runs. 2) Defined fallback policy (kernel, quantization, prefill throttling) that reduces 95th percentile decode latency by >=25% in regression cases. 3) Canary rollout automation and alert thresholds added to the runtime pipeline. 4) Runbook updated with rollback steps and postmortem checklist.
background: Context: In the last v3 pilot we moved to a preference for FA3 kernels for medium-long sequences. A small but significant portion of traffic (multi-turn chat with pinned prompts) experienced prefilling pressure that led to workspace contention during the first decode tokens. Existing kernel-prober and warmup shims smooth steady-state choice but do not faithfully emulate eviction dynamics during startup bursts. Ops reported 3 customer incidents (internal IDs linked in comments) and a couple of GitHub PRs that attempted mitigations but lacked reliable repro and metrics.
plan: 1) Implement an eviction emulator that simulates workspace allocation, delayed KV cache materialization, and staggered microbatch handoffs. 2) Instrument emulator with fine-grained telemetry: per-kernel memory high-watermarks, prefill completion times, time-to-first-token, and per-token latency distribution. 3) Use emulator to evaluate candidate fallback policies: a) degrade to FA2-like kernel layout for first N tokens, b) prefix-level throttling (microbatch pacing), c) transient quantization for startup path. 4) Produce a canary plan with traffic sampling and automatic rollback triggers. 5) Commit runtime changes behind a feature flag and run a 72h canary with monitored SLOs.
test_plan: - Unit tests for emulator correctness (deterministic allocation sequences). - Microbench scenarios matching customer traces (links in comments). - CI perf matrix across GPUs (A100/4090/MI250) for both v2 and v3 kernels. - Nightly long-context stress job to detect oscillation between kernels and measure percent of runs that hit fallback. - Canary: 0.5% traffic for 24h -> 2% for 48h -> 10% for 72h with automated rollback on SLO violation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Emulator may not capture multi-tenant interference. Mitigation: Add a noise-injection mode that simulates background alloc/free churn. Risk: Fallback adds cost due to lower throughput. Mitigation: Use staged, token-limited fallback (only first 16 tokens) and track cost delta in per-route metrics.

2025-02-18 - Marcus Liu: POC eviction emulator committed to branch 'evict-emulator/poc' - reproduces tail-latency locally using a condensed trace from INC-2025-0214. Observed similar 95th latency delta (~34%).

2025-02-21 - Elena Martín (SRE reviewer): Reviewed POC telemetry. Suggested adding 'time-to-first-kv-materialize' metric and a noise-injection mode to emulate noisy multi-tenant activity. Marked as 'needs follow-up'.

2025-02-25 - Marcus Liu: Implemented noise-injection and added memory high-watermark counters. Bench runs across A100 show that a 'first-16-token fallback to fa2-layout' reduces 95th by ~28% on the repro trace. CPU-side cost delta estimated at +6% token-cost for those flows.

2025-03-01 - Product: Priya Shah: Reviewed trade-offs. Approved token-limited fallback approach for canary given customer-impact medium and small cost increase. Requested explicit customer notification plan for affected routes.

2025-03-03 - Marcus Liu: Canary automation draft: sample routes via runtime-router, attach 'eviction-fallback' feature flag. Alert if 95th latency increases by >10% vs baseline or error rate increases by >0.1% for 15m window. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5012
